one_sentence_story: Stepping through a door tells your brain to file the old room and make space for the new one.
so_what_for_you: Blanking in the kitchen doorway does not mean a bad memory. Carry a small cue in your hand or say one word out loud before you step into the next room.

jargon_map.plain: Forgetting what you came for right after you step into a new room.
jargon_map.analogy: Like closing one browser tab and forgetting what to type next.

jargon_map.plain: Your brain splits each day into neat room-sized chapters.
jargon_map.analogy: Like starting a fresh page each time you change scenes.

jargon_map.plain: Memory cells that fire a quick pulse when you cross into a new space.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a camera shutter clicking to save the last room.

jargon_map.plain: Trying to hold too many errands in your head at the same time.
jargon_map.analogy: Carrying four full coffee mugs through a swinging door.
